scope: Secrecy/privacy and quantum Shannon bridges, with exact finite-dimensional quantum library suppliers
snapshot_method: Inspected current published page frontmatter and referenced item files; searched items/ and library/ for entropy, relative entropy, Holevo, accessible information, quantum channel capacity, private capacity and coherent information.

items.clauses_used: Defines finite Shannon entropy and finite KL divergence with 0 ln 0 = 0, support failure +infinity, row-stochastic matrices, and natural-log units.
Defines directional measurable-space KL via Radon-Nikodym derivatives, with absolute-continuity support condition and well-defined extended integral.
Defines mutual information only for a finite uniform hypothesis J with general observation law; it is not a general finite-alphabet I(X;Y) definition.

existing_suppliers.interface_note: Wilde uses log base 2. Reuse the natural-log suppliers by multiplying by 1/ln(2), or state the base-2 definition locally. No full general discrete mutual-information item was found.

existing_suppliers.clauses_used: Positive trace-one state on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex space; support is the orthogonal complement of kernel; ensemble barycentres and purification exist; Schmidt and spectral decompositions are finite.

existing_suppliers.topic: Registers, tensor products and partial trace
existing_suppliers.clauses_used: Finite factor order and basis are fixed; the partial trace is basis independent, positive and trace preserving; finite trace pairing is nondegenerate. The empty tensor product is C; a state is not defined on the zero-dimensional space.

A finite-dimensional channel is complex-linear, CP under every finite ancillary amplification, and TP on every operator. TP Kraus normalization is sum K_a dagger K_a = I. A chosen finite Kraus family supplies an isometric Stinespring dilation; its environment output defines a finite complementary channel.

Finite nonempty outcomes, positive effects summing to identity, p(a)=Tr(rho E_a), CP branch maps, normalized positive-probability conditional states, explicit null handling for zero-probability branches.

existing_suppliers.topic: State distinguishability, fidelity and channel norms
existing_suppliers.clauses_used: D(rho,sigma)=one-half ||rho-sigma||_1; equal-prior Helstrom success is (1+D)/2; finite POVM outcome variation is at most D; trace distance contracts under finite CPTP maps; root fidelity is unsquared; diamond norm on maps is unhalved; channel hybrid/tensor error sums have finite-dimensional scope.

existing_suppliers.topic: Coding and exact quantum error recovery
existing_suppliers.clauses_used: Finite-register code subspaces, error detection, exact Knill-Laflamme recovery, teleportation and dense-coding unit protocols. These are not channel-capacity theorems.

For independent integrable variables Xi in deterministic finite intervals [ai,bi], thm-hoeffding-independent-bounded-sums gives P(|sum(Xi-EXi)|>=t)<=2 exp(-2t^2/sum_i(bi-ai)^2), with the zero-width case explicit. It applies to finite-family conditional surprisal variables coordinate by coordinate; no iid assumption is needed.

not_currently_supplied_in_library: Finite von Neumann entropy and its joint/conditional entropy identities for density operators.
Finite Umegaki quantum relative entropy with support convention and data-processing proof.
Strong subadditivity and quantum conditional mutual information nonnegativity.
Finite cq Holevo information, accessible information and the measurement/Holevo inequality.
HSW regularized classical capacity, entanglement-assisted classical capacity, quantum private capacity, quantum capacity and dynamic-capacity coding theorems.
Composable real/ideal QKD security definition, abort handling, correctness/secrecy split and composition theorem.

not_suppliers.reason: Proves data processing only for trace distance under finite CPTP maps; it does not establish Umegaki relative-entropy DPI.
Controls diamond-norm error of channel composition; it is not an information-capacity or entropy-additivity theorem.
The category page is currently draft and contains no accepted entropy, Holevo or channel-capacity supplier.

local_proof_obligations_for_scaffold.contract: For a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex space, define S(rho)=-Tr(rho log2 rho), using spectral functional calculus and 0 log 0=0. Prove basis independence and finite well-definedness from the existing finite spectral theorem and trace.

Define D(rho||sigma)=Tr rho(log2 rho-log2 sigma) for PSD/density operators when supp(rho) subset supp(sigma), and +infinity otherwise. Define logarithms on positive support and explicitly establish support inclusion for every later use.
For T>0 and isometry V, prove V*(T+sI)^(-1)V >= (V*TV+sI)^(-1) by the variational formula for a positive inverse.
Derive the finite-matrix -log integral representation and integrate inverse compression with finite cutoffs, then pass to the norm limit; do not assume a global operator-Jensen result.
On the finite Hilbert-Schmidt operator space define left multiplication by B and right multiplication by A^(-1); diagonalize on matrix units |b_j><a_i| to derive the entropy identity.
For finite families A_i,B_i>0 and positive weights summing to one, construct an isometry of Hilbert-Schmidt spaces and use the -log compression inequality.

Prove D(A+epsilon I||B+epsilon I) tends to the support-defined D(A||B), including +infinity exactly when supp(A) is not contained in supp(B). This is a particular regularization limit, not global continuity.
Extend positive-definite joint convexity to PSD pairs by common epsilon I regularization and the proved support limit; omit zero weights.
In finite positive dimension d, prove by matrix-unit summation the identity Weyl twirl R -> Tr_B(R) tensor I_B/d and handle d=1 separately.
Combine finite Weyl twirling, unitary invariance and joint convexity, checking support-inclusion and +infinity cases.

Use the published finite Stinespring dilation, isometric invariance from finite spectra, and partial-trace DPI. State nonzero finite input/output dimensions and PSD support hypotheses explicitly; no recovery equality follows.
Apply finite relative-entropy DPI to (rho_ABC, rho_A tensor rho_BC) under Tr_C, prove support inclusion for the product reference first, and expand finite entropies to obtain I(A;C|B)>=0.

Define the finite cq block state and prove its entropy identity by listing eigenvalues. Apply finite CPTP relative-entropy or mutual-information DPI to a POVM measurement channel; optimize over finite POVMs for accessible information.

coordination_note: The inverse-compression/resolvent/joint-convexity/Weyl-twirl ladder is the independent auditor's proof contract in audit/independent-proof-notes.md, section Quantum relative-entropy DPI: finite-dimensional resolvent ladder. It is the recommended basic DPI/SSA route. Wilde's recovery theorem remains a separate advanced consumer.
